I got this, hoping that the extra data provided would allow me to gain insight onto how to deal with stress. The stress score is really don’t match with how my body feels either physically or mentally. I can have an extremely difficult day at work and it gives me a low stress score. I can have an easy day at work and have a hard workout it gives me a high stress score.

Those two things are very different and how my body feels them. Additionally, the most stressful day at work can have a score of 4.2 and a 30 minute ride at 60% heart rate gives a 4.2 score. Those are extremely different issues. 

Also, it is difficult to understand because the scores don’t really jibe or relate to how you’re feeling. It produces a lot of data, but I’m not sure if it’s actually reliable or accurate so it’s not worth the extra money or commitment to wearing it at night.

Many people complain about the cost of Whoop, but I find that I get great data and insights from the app and the AI interface. It really helps me understand my recovery from exercise, how well I’m sleeping, how my eating patterns affect my sleep and recovery. It’s been really great.

The Whoop is an interesting tool that helped me to gain valuable insight regarding my sleep and training. After a couple of months I feel it no longer serves it purpose. I’d return it and save the $27 per month but I am committed to one year so that’s not an option. It is an expensive toy, for what I need. Looks good.

I love my Whoop band! It helps me to stay motivated and gives me clear insights into my health. The AI is getting better and they are putting a lot of effort into developing the product/app more.

My main issues are is that I feel like there are multiple features that you would think are basic features for a health device that are missing. For example, I have to track activities twice. Once in the actual activity section and then another time in my daily journal. It seems like the activity section should automatically update the Journal so you don’t have to repeat efforts speaking of the activity section, there are times where it misses the activity that I’m doing, especially low strength, activities like blah, blah blah, remember there are times when I’m sitting on the couch and open my app to 15 potential activity spotted messages. Also, the app doesn’t track basic things like blood oxygen levels throughout the day. Want to see the average lifespan of your battery? Sorry, can’t see that. Wanna ask the AI the average length of your dog walks, running, or other physical activity? Sorry, even though it attracts the data attracts your route, you are unable to see this either. Lastly, all the replacement bands are $100 or more. My band that I have now, which is my original band that I came with, desperately needs to be replaced, but because there are no cost-effective replacement I have yet to pull the trigger.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. I love the band, which is fairly comfortable and looks good, the WHOOP support team are very responsive and efficient, who is amazing at giving you daily strained targets that feel accurate and attainable, but still push you for training, and the app does genuinely encourage me to look at it each day, which helps with me staying consistent with my daily goals. I do really like the way. The AI is developing as well, being more responsive and being able to help with setting goals and adjusting goals as necessary based on what’s going on in life. 

Well, there are a lot of things that need to be developed or fixed, I would still highly recommend the WHOOP to anybody looking for a Fitness device. The speed at which WHOOP developing their app and product gives me hope that the things that I’m asking for will one day soon be features and overall I really do love my WHOOP band. I would probably recommend it best for those who are already moderately active and looking to bring their fitness to the next level, those looking to track and maintain daily habits, or those who generally want more insights into their health. I do still think that other brands might be better for women looking to track their cycles in fertility, or for those who don’t want to wait for the features that I mentioned above.

I’ve really enjoyed using WHOOP overall, but there are a few areas where I think it could be significantly better.

What I love:

The UI/UX is excellent. The app feels modern, sleek, and very tech-forward. I genuinely enjoy going through it every morning because everything is intuitive, easy to understand, and presented in a way that feels premium. WHOOP does a great job taking a lot of health and fitness data and making it approachable without feeling overwhelming.

I’ve also been impressed with the Recovery score. Most mornings, my recovery has lined up surprisingly well with how I actually feel when I wake up. That’s probably the feature I’ve found most valuable.

Where it falls short:

The WHOOP Coach/AI needs improvement. There have been times when its recommendations didn’t seem to match either my recovery data or how I was feeling. One morning I woke up feeling pretty run down with a 50% yellow recovery, yet WHOOP Coach essentially told me to train as usual. Bevel, using much of the same underlying health data, recommended that I take it easy and prioritize recovery. I followed Bevel’s recommendation, rested, and had a great recovery score the following day.

Obviously, one example doesn’t prove one recommendation was definitively better, but it made me much less confident in WHOOP Coach. For a product built so heavily around recovery, I’d like the AI to be more conservative and context-aware when recovery is mediocre and the user reports feeling poorly.

Sleep detection has also been disappointing compared with my Apple Watch. One night this past week, I was awake for roughly two hours in the middle of the night. My Apple Watch correctly detected that extended period of wakefulness, while WHOOP essentially treated it as a near-perfect night of sleep. That’s a pretty significant miss for a device where sleep is such an important part of the overall experience and Recovery score. For the amount of money Whoop costs you’d think the sleep detection would be on par with the Apple Watch. 

Overall, I really like WHOOP. The design, presentation of data, and Recovery experience are some of the best I’ve used. But for me, the AI coaching and sleep/wake detection need to catch up with the rest of the product. If WHOOP can improve those two areas, the overall experience would be much harder to beat. For the price I’d expect better quality. Especially since there are other apps that do similar things for less money.

I purchased the lifetime membership because I have high blood pressure and wanted a device to help me track it. I was very disappointed to learn that Whoop does not measure or even estimate your blood pressure. Instead, it asks you to manually enter your blood pressure readings and then simply shows the average of the values you entered yourself.

There is no real blood pressure monitoring, no estimated readings, and no meaningful tracking beyond your own manual entries. If blood pressure is your main concern, this device will not meet your expectations. I believe this limitation should be made much clearer before customers purchase a membership.

WHOOP is easily the best hardware in the market. It just sits on your wrist and silently collects data for about a week without a charge – perfect. 

BUT it’s designed for one audience - pro athletes.  They don’t offer different workflows for wellness or health tracking, and that’s incredibly limiting.

The dashboard delivers a daily verdict that can feel harsh if you’re managing a chronic health issue (if you’re on heart medication that impacts HRV for example). 

If you can look past the dashboards, the underlying data is incredible. On a personal level, it’s been transformative but it’s difficult to access. WHOOP only syncs a narrow set of fields to Apple health, so it’s difficult to share data with my provider or with AI tools like Claude for deeper insights. 

I understand the goal is to keep the user within the WHOOP ecosystem, but the embedded AI tool isn’t useful. It can’t connect to external resources or support uploaded documents for ongoing reference – it can only surface basic responses to the dashboard.  I’m also not interested in paying for health tests and bloodwork when they’re covered under my health insurance policy through my provider, I can’t imagine most people are….

I’ve really enjoyed using WHOOP overall, but there are a few areas where I think it could be significantly better.

What I love:

The UI/UX is excellent. The app feels modern, sleek, and very tech-forward. I genuinely enjoy going through it every morning because everything is intuitive, easy to understand, and presented in a way that feels premium. WHOOP does a great job taking a lot of health and fitness data and making it approachable without feeling overwhelming.

I’ve also been impressed with the Recovery score. Most mornings, my recovery has lined up surprisingly well with how I actually feel when I wake up. That’s probably the feature I’ve found most valuable.

Where it falls short:

The WHOOP Coach/AI needs improvement. There have been times when its recommendations didn’t seem to match either my recovery data or how I was feeling. One morning I woke up feeling pretty run down with a 50% yellow recovery, yet WHOOP Coach essentially told me to train as usual. Bevel, using much of the same underlying health data, recommended that I take it easy and prioritize recovery. I followed Bevel’s recommendation, rested, and had a great recovery score the following day.

Obviously, one example doesn’t prove one recommendation was definitively better, but it made me much less confident in WHOOP Coach. For a product built so heavily around recovery, I’d like the AI to be more conservative and context-aware when recovery is mediocre and the user reports feeling poorly.

Sleep detection has also been disappointing compared with my Apple Watch. One night this past week, I was awake for roughly two hours in the middle of the night. My Apple Watch correctly detected that extended period of wakefulness, while WHOOP essentially treated it as a near-perfect night of sleep. That’s a pretty significant miss for a device where sleep is such an important part of the overall experience and Recovery score. For the amount of money Whoop costs you’d think the sleep detection would be on par with the Apple Watch. 

Overall, I really like WHOOP. The design, presentation of data, and Recovery experience are some of the best I’ve used. But for me, the AI coaching and sleep/wake detection need to catch up with the rest of the product. If WHOOP can improve those two areas, the overall experience would be much harder to beat. For the price I’d expect better quality. Especially since there are other apps that do similar things for less money.

I’ve really enjoyed using WHOOP overall, but there are a few areas where I think it could be significantly better.

What I love:

The UI/UX is excellent. The app feels modern, sleek, and very tech-forward. I genuinely enjoy going through it every morning because everything is intuitive, easy to understand, and presented in a way that feels premium. WHOOP does a great job taking a lot of health and fitness data and making it approachable without feeling overwhelming.

I’ve also been impressed with the Recovery score. Most mornings, my recovery has lined up surprisingly well with how I actually feel when I wake up. That’s probably the feature I’ve found most valuable.

Where it falls short:

The WHOOP Coach/AI needs improvement. There have been times when its recommendations didn’t seem to match either my recovery data or how I was feeling. One morning I woke up feeling pretty run down with a 50% yellow recovery, yet WHOOP Coach essentially told me to train as usual. Bevel, using much of the same underlying health data, recommended that I take it easy and prioritize recovery. I followed Bevel’s recommendation, rested, and had a great recovery score the following day.

Obviously, one example doesn’t prove one recommendation was definitively better, but it made me much less confident in WHOOP Coach. For a product built so heavily around recovery, I’d like the AI to be more conservative and context-aware when recovery is mediocre and the user reports feeling poorly.

Sleep detection has also been disappointing compared with my Apple Watch. One night this past week, I was awake for roughly two hours in the middle of the night. My Apple Watch correctly detected that extended period of wakefulness, while WHOOP essentially treated it as a near-perfect night of sleep. That’s a pretty significant miss for a device where sleep is such an important part of the overall experience and Recovery score. For the amount of money Whoop costs you’d think the sleep detection would be on par with the Apple Watch. 

Overall, I really like WHOOP. The design, presentation of data, and Recovery experience are some of the best I’ve used. But for me, the AI coaching and sleep/wake detection need to catch up with the rest of the product. If WHOOP can improve those two areas, the overall experience would be much harder to beat. For the price I’d expect better quality. Especially since there are other apps that do similar things for less money.

I have both a new apple watch and a new whoop, so I can compare them. Whoop is great for sleep and recovery due to its long-lasting battery. The Apple watch, with its 1-day battery, is not usable since you need to charge it every night.  Whoop has accurately validated its model for determining heart in steady state situations like running and sleeping.  

But it’s model is not satisfactory for strength training.  I have done tests where I do an intense lifting set that brings me to a high heart rate (145bpm) where i am breathing rapidly and then slowly my heart rate decreases over 3 minutes to 95 bpm. the apple watch correctly follows the trend. the whoop instead stays at 95bpm this whole time.  This is because it is using a conservative algorithm for recording only “good heart beats”.  When strength training, the heart beats do not match its criteria, and it reverts to its previous measurements before the lifting started.  This is not satisfactory.  You would think if you are doing a “strength training session” in whoop, it would adjust and allow for large heart rate changes.  But this apparently is not a priority for them.

WHOOP is better than Oura Ring and Apple Watch for weight training because it is designed to be worn during lifting and to actually quantify strength work, not just detect that a workout happened. Oura advises removing its ring during weightlifting due to friction and damage risk, which makes it impractical for consistent strength-training tracking. Apple Watch can record strength workouts, but detailed logging of sets, reps, and weight typically relies on third-party apps, and its battery life (about a day) makes continuous recovery and strain tracking harder. In contrast, WHOOP’s Strength Trainer is built specifically for resistance training, allowing users to log exercises, sets, reps, and weight and translating that data into a muscular load and overall strain score, while its multi-day battery life supports uninterrupted 24/7 wear.

The WHOOP was the first/only wearable that I found to track my strain/HRV in the weight room. I started with gen 2 and have used every version except the WHOOP Life. I have the 5.0 MG, and all throughout my use of the WHOOP, I have been hoping for updates to the strength trainer section of the app. I provide tons of feedback anytime I get a survey. They have never improved the UI of the strength trainer section, and it’s THE ONLY THING that sets this expensive wearable apart from my Garmin. Well, not anymore now that Garmin tracks strength training. Additionally, one of the key elements of the expense was that you would never have to pay for upgrades. You paid ~$450/year, so you get them. Not with the 5.0! The band is minutely smaller, so I have to get all new accessories because all the others don’t fit anymore; the charger won’t fit from my 4.0; the WHOOP 5.0 (not even considering the life/MG) is a costly “one-time” charge; and the strength training section still isn’t upgraded! I give this product zero stars because it is a low-quality device—cheap, inaccurate, unreliable, and simply not fit for purpose.

From the first day, I reported serious issues with core features such as ECG and blood pressure, which do not work at all. These are not minor features—they are exactly why someone would pay for a WHOOP membership. Despite raising these issues early, nothing was fixed.

Basic functionality is also unacceptable. I walk around 10,000 steps daily, yet the device records nothing while I am walking unless I manually log the activity. That completely defeats the purpose of using a wearable tracker.

The overall experience feels like using a product that is far behind the market standard, both in hardware quality and software performance. It is nowhere near the level of competitors like Apple Watch or Oura.

Customer support makes things worse. Responses is an AI automated and repetitive, with no real effort to resolve the actual problem. Instead of fixing issues, they redirect to generic troubleshooting steps that do not work.

WHOOP even granted me an additional one-month credit, which clearly acknowledges there were unresolved issues. Yet when I requested a refund, they refused, relying strictly on policy rather than addressing the fact that the product never worked properly from the start.

In summary:
	•Core features do not function properly
	•Tracking is highly inaccurate
	•Product quality is poor
	•Support is inhuman and ineffective and unhelpful
	•Refund handling is unfair

I purchased WHOOP expecting a premium product and premium service, but my experience has been frustrating from the very beginning.

After only a few days of use, the app stopped working properly. One morning, my recovery never processed, the app remained stuck on the previous day, and my data would not update correctly. For a product that is supposed to provide real-time health and recovery insights, this is unacceptable.

The customer service experience has been equally frustrating. Finding support is difficult, getting help takes too long, and there is no simple way to resolve issues quickly.

The return process is another major problem. Customers are expected to pay for return shipping, and accessories cannot be returned through a simple online process. Instead, you have to contact customer support first, which is unnecessarily complicated and time-consuming.

For a company charging premium prices and a membership fee, I expected a polished product, reliable software, and responsive customer support. Instead, I experienced app issues within the first week, poor customer service, and a frustrating return process.

This has been one of the worst experiences I’ve had with a wearable technology company, and I would not recommend WHOOP to others.

I got this, hoping that the extra data provided would allow me to gain insight onto how to deal with stress. The stress score is really don’t match with how my body feels either physically or mentally. I can have an extremely difficult day at work and it gives me a low stress score. I can have an easy day at work and have a hard workout it gives me a high stress score.

Those two things are very different and how my body feels them. Additionally, the most stressful day at work can have a score of 4.2 and a 30 minute ride at 60% heart rate gives a 4.2 score. Those are extremely different issues. 

Also, it is difficult to understand because the scores don’t really jibe or relate to how you’re feeling. It produces a lot of data, but I’m not sure if it’s actually reliable or accurate so it’s not worth the extra money or commitment to wearing it at night.
During this time, I haven’t been satisfied with the step counter or strain data. There were days when I hadn’t even gotten out of bed yet, but it had already recorded 1,600 steps.

I love my Whoop band! It helps me to stay motivated and gives me clear insights into my health. The AI is getting better and they are putting a lot of effort into developing the product/app more.

My main issues are is that I feel like there are multiple features that you would think are basic features for a health device that are missing. For example, I have to track activities twice. Once in the actual activity section and then another time in my daily journal. It seems like the activity section should automatically update the Journal so you don’t have to repeat efforts speaking of the activity section, there are times where it misses the activity that I’m doing, especially low strength, activities like blah, blah blah, remember there are times when I’m sitting on the couch and open my app to 15 potential activity spotted messages. Also, the app doesn’t track basic things like blood oxygen levels throughout the day. Want to see the average lifespan of your battery? Sorry, can’t see that. Wanna ask the AI the average length of your dog walks, running, or other physical activity? Sorry, even though it attracts the data attracts your route, you are unable to see this either. Lastly, all the replacement bands are $100 or more. My band that I have now, which is my original band that I came with, desperately needs to be replaced, but because there are no cost-effective replacement I have yet to pull the trigger.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. I love the band, which is fairly comfortable and looks good, the WHOOP support team are very responsive and efficient, who is amazing at giving you daily strained targets that feel accurate and attainable, but still push you for training, and the app does genuinely encourage me to look at it each day, which helps with me staying consistent with my daily goals. I do really like the way. The AI is developing as well, being more responsive and being able to help with setting goals and adjusting goals as necessary based on what’s going on in life. 

Well, there are a lot of things that need to be developed or fixed, I would still highly recommend the WHOOP to anybody looking for a Fitness device. The speed at which WHOOP developing their app and product gives me hope that the things that I’m asking for will one day soon be features and overall I really do love my WHOOP band. I would probably recommend it best for those who are already moderately active and looking to bring their fitness to the next level, those looking to track and maintain daily habits, or those who generally want more insights into their health. I do still think that other brands might be better for women looking to track their cycles in fertility, or for those who don’t want to wait for the features that I mentioned above.

Since upgrading to the new WHOOP, the changes to the algorithm have made my Strain and calorie data feel completely inaccurate. My calories burned are now around 30% lower than before. Walks sometimes register no Strain, and even after an intense weightlifting session plus 15–20k steps, my calories barely show above BMR. It’s incredibly frustrating and affects my confidence in the overall health data. I really hope WHOOP fixes this soon.

I’m a very active middle aged person who adopted Whoop to track my multitude of activities. I’ve encountered a major problem: Whoop doesn’t accurately measure where most of us live our lives: in HR zones 0-2. For a 5 mile walk in 85*F heat, whoop recorded 150 calories. Why? ‘I wasn’t working hard enough.’ The AI agent was condescending, passive aggressive and deflective. So, if you aren’t regularly pushing yourself often at HR zones 4-5, Whoop is basically useless for you.

I have been wearing in my room for four years now and it just keeps me on track. I love the fact that it tells me if I could work out again basically in my recovery or if I’m overworking myself. But my biggest thing is keeping up with my HRV and my resting heart rate in my sleep. I have worn Fitbit and Garmin and WHOOP is my absolute favorite as far as accuracy.

The concept sounds amazing. Monitor your vitals and help you improve performance and health. Other than the strain monitor, the other metrics are questionable at best. And the AI Chatbot, which is supposed to give you advice is utterly useless.. You are way better off to just talk with Claude or ChatGPT then waste your time with Whoop.

The piling on of AI “features” that I can’t turn off or opt out of is already irritating, but the tracking has also only been getting worse (it used to be on the nose about my main activity, now it is all over the place and regular automatically stops logging when I’ve barely even started, only to log showers as activities instead). It might just be coincidence but the decline coinciding with the increased AI integration, and my observations of every other AI tool I’ve been unable to avoid, do make me suspicious that these things are related, to Whoop’s detriment. A new low, it logged 4x as many steps as Apple Health today - I was on a road trip for 5.5 hours, Whoop is definitely the one that’s wrong about this. If they insist on burying themselves with AI, I just wish I could at least turn off the way it interacts with me. I don’t want an app talking to me in a creepy imitation of a person. Unfortunately, I bought a longer subscription at my last renewal. If the accuracy doesn’t come back by the time that expires, I just don’t think the high price will be worth it.

I’m not sure MG for medical grade necessarily means anything beyond Marketing. I’m cautiously optimistic.

I like the Data. sometimes the Data collection can be abehrrent but typically spot in for trends. wish subscription tiered down (ie less as time goes on until nothing. would be a good model as competitors are coming)

activity_detection.text: Unobtrusive but buggy. The band is comfortable and doesn't intrude on day to day activities. The app has a lot of good info but seems to miss detecting exercise activities several times per week. When I manually add the activity, the app inconsistently records and displays the results. I wear the band consistently and never shut the app off. Seems to be a data sync issue leading into a record issue.

This app used to detect activities, naps, and helped me track my period after years of tracking it on other apps. Now none of those things happen, weight and periods are not recorded same with activities and naps. The metrics aren’t even correct. Don’t waste you’re money it’s all marketing and a scam
It used to label activities correctly after detecting them. Now it doesn’t. Support staff doesn’t seem to care after going back and fourth in the issue.

I love my Whoop band! It helps me to stay motivated and gives me clear insights into my health. The AI is getting better and they are putting a lot of effort into developing the product/app more.

My main issues are is that I feel like there are multiple features that you would think are basic features for a health device that are missing. For example, I have to track activities twice. Once in the actual activity section and then another time in my daily journal. It seems like the activity section should automatically update the Journal so you don’t have to repeat efforts speaking of the activity section, there are times where it misses the activity that I’m doing, especially low strength, activities like blah, blah blah, remember there are times when I’m sitting on the couch and open my app to 15 potential activity spotted messages. Also, the app doesn’t track basic things like blood oxygen levels throughout the day. Want to see the average lifespan of your battery? Sorry, can’t see that. Wanna ask the AI the average length of your dog walks, running, or other physical activity? Sorry, even though it attracts the data attracts your route, you are unable to see this either. Lastly, all the replacement bands are $100 or more. My band that I have now, which is my original band that I came with, desperately needs to be replaced, but because there are no cost-effective replacement I have yet to pull the trigger.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. I love the band, which is fairly comfortable and looks good, the WHOOP support team are very responsive and efficient, who is amazing at giving you daily strained targets that feel accurate and attainable, but still push you for training, and the app does genuinely encourage me to look at it each day, which helps with me staying consistent with my daily goals. I do really like the way. The AI is developing as well, being more responsive and being able to help with setting goals and adjusting goals as necessary based on what’s going on in life. 

Well, there are a lot of things that need to be developed or fixed, I would still highly recommend the WHOOP to anybody looking for a Fitness device. The speed at which WHOOP developing their app and product gives me hope that the things that I’m asking for will one day soon be features and overall I really do love my WHOOP band. I would probably recommend it best for those who are already moderately active and looking to bring their fitness to the next level, those looking to track and maintain daily habits, or those who generally want more insights into their health. I do still think that other brands might be better for women looking to track their cycles in fertility, or for those who don’t want to wait for the features that I mentioned above.

Since upgrading to the new WHOOP, the changes to the algorithm have made my Strain and calorie data feel completely inaccurate. My calories burned are now around 30% lower than before. Walks sometimes register no Strain, and even after an intense weightlifting session plus 15–20k steps, my calories barely show above BMR. It’s incredibly frustrating and affects my confidence in the overall health data. I really hope WHOOP fixes this soon.

The piling on of AI “features” that I can’t turn off or opt out of is already irritating, but the tracking has also only been getting worse (it used to be on the nose about my main activity, now it is all over the place and regular automatically stops logging when I’ve barely even started, only to log showers as activities instead). It might just be coincidence but the decline coinciding with the increased AI integration, and my observations of every other AI tool I’ve been unable to avoid, do make me suspicious that these things are related, to Whoop’s detriment. A new low, it logged 4x as many steps as Apple Health today - I was on a road trip for 5.5 hours, Whoop is definitely the one that’s wrong about this. If they insist on burying themselves with AI, I just wish I could at least turn off the way it interacts with me. I don’t want an app talking to me in a creepy imitation of a person. Unfortunately, I bought a longer subscription at my last renewal. If the accuracy doesn’t come back by the time that expires, I just don’t think the high price will be worth it.
Somtimes the app dosent recognize the nap ,timing your workout and counting steps
useless. most of my activities don't show results because the sensor stops working. when it works, 1h intense runs shows less strain than 10 minute slow walk. uselss

Monitoring of sleep and recovery ,HRV ,are very good. But many rooms of improvement for the expensive cost of memberships. Ai advice are mainly push you to more exercise and sleep. And data collections , diary are time consuming. It cannot detect activities uncless you log in. customer service are slow. Multiple lag time and hang of app requiring forced close and restore. Ai advice of activities are not medical advice , but its act like one. So I use it just baseline daily monitor.

it is kind of fun, but I suspect it makes up data sometimes, and it is really bad at offline data capture. If you're going on a multiday hike out of coverage, Whoop will fail to capture your activities. It needs some work

relax practice not work without network connection, whoop simultaneously disconnected from app, activity auto-detection worx bad, stupid time input interface when filling out the journal — it's impossible to get to the right time (previous review magically deleted from store)

It’s cool to see the tracking for like simple workouts and jogs, but if you do intense physical contact sports like mma it does a horrible job of tracking your stats. I have had multiple sessions where it just gives me a blank time period when I’m working out and it’s very frustrating. Sometimes it works but it’s very in consistent. Also the price is so much for something so simple. Buying an Apple Watch is the same thing but no subscription.
Misses workouts, messes up sleep! The AI brain is the size of an acorn that’s been flattened by a 18 wheeler truck!

Somehow the activity detection and sleep tracking has gotten worse over the last six months.  Getting notifications about playing golf when walking, exercise while driving and just general weirdness.  Also the sleep detection and tracking needs a ton of improvement.  Like the idea, product is just not there yet.

I like the metrics and insights, but the AI has significant limitations. It creates problems it cannot undo. It logged strength training as indoor cycling. It logged indoor rowing as outdoor rowing. And it’s on me to report the bugs. This is beta tech at best.

Really do I take naps but I’ve taken two in the last month and the WHOOP doesn’t even detect the nap, but my Apple Watch does.  Then I manually added it in the apps and somehow it makes up data of deep sleep, light sleep… Etc.
It has my HRV in the 20s. Yet, when I have worn other. Devices, including the Apple Watch Ultra, I’m in the 40s 50s and sometimes 70s because the Apple Watch measures it throughout the day at different times. 
I exercise six days a week. Sometimes I go for runs, and it doesn’t detect the run. I have to manually input it and then it makes up which zone I was in all of a sudden.  The same with lifting weights, I always have to insert the data manually.  
I took my blood pressure three times and input the data. When I take my blood pressure manually with the arm wrap the whoop isn’t close most of the time.   I get that it takes your blood pressure in the middle of the night but I don’t see this being a blood pressure device.  
I have visited with three different doctors and all of them say the Apple Watch is the best and they have gone to medical conferences and the discussion has come up and  the Apple Watch is always discussed as being the most accurate.  
What you’re buying with the WHOOP is a glorified nighttime sleep tracker.  
I’m sure people love their WHOOP and I know they have a cult following   
If you’re thinking about getting it, save your money and just wear your Apple Watch or your Google watch  
Honestly, if you get a good nights sleep, you eat right and you exercise you don’t even need one of these device to track stuff   
Just pay attention to what your body tells you with how you feel

Been using Whoop for 4 months religiously and have had nothing but frustration with the faulty data and bad AI coaching.  Zero improvement in sleep and horrible workout plans with the strength trainer.  You’ll go for a run and 10 minutes later get a notification asking if you’re going to go for a run…it’s so frustrating.  I want my money back but I’m stuck with it.

Nothing meaningful has been added to the app in so long. The device constantly logs workouts incorrectly - I just vacuumed and it thought I was weightlifting. This used to be a cutting edge company and now it’s average. This is not worth the exorbitant price tag, and I will not be renewing my subscription.
works well, logs activity automatically...but keeps thinking im playing baseball when I am just walking around at work. you can't customize the activities

I hope it gets better or I will be looking for an alternative. :-(

Whoop app is great. Only problems have to do with activity recognition and sometimes sleep tracking (but only because I often have to wake up in the middle of the night and get to work- then come back home to sleep) five stars after 3 years

Even simple features like automatic time zone changes or ending a workout automatically — or at least notifying you when your heart rate drops — don’t work properly. Save your money and buy something that actually works.

Not sure if their software needs ti be fixed or their device has issues, the support team doesn’t know that either.

Whoop caught my slightly elevated skin temperature from Lyme disease before I knew I was sick; urgent care used the data to help diagnose and treat me. Whoop then helped guide me through reconditioning to full recovery. More important: it caught my husband’s serious but hard to track symptoms that were eventually diagnosed as lymphoma. Whoop is not just a health monitor and fitness coach, it is a life-saver.

I do not recommend the Whoop band if you’re buying it for blood pressure monitoring.

I purchased the lifetime membership because I have high blood pressure and wanted a device to help me track it. I was very disappointed to learn that Whoop does not measure or even estimate your blood pressure. Instead, it asks you to manually enter your blood pressure readings and then simply shows the average of the values you entered yourself.

There is no real blood pressure monitoring, no estimated readings, and no meaningful tracking beyond your own manual entries. If blood pressure is your main concern, this device will not meet your expectations. I believe this limitation should be made much clearer before customers purchase a membership.

I’ve used whoop for about 6 years now and it’s changed my life. Knowing my metrics and being able to adjust to optimize my fitness shaped my journey post college sports. Not every day is a push day and whoop’s recovery features help me know when my body needs rest, so I don’t feel as if I’m just being lazy. Also so many new features like ECG, daily blood pressure readings, and whoop’s AI is such an intelligent use to better your health as opposed to ignorantly using AI to create memes and ask it silly things. I also participate in every study whoop has offered me, I love that they advance science. On top of scientific discovery, it also makes their product more accurate in the time I’ve used it (a big perk of the product is the accuracy). While the pricepoint is higher, as a preventative medicine professional (I’m an RN in biometric screenings) I firmly believe they are giving you sound data to improve your health day in and day out & make it well worth the price.

I recently got this device, it’s been 47 days. Since day 1: I have been unable to access the health page. I am on a 17 pro and the moment I open the health tab and slide down, it crashes. The app becomes unresponsive. I have emailed whoop several times about it, to only get AI responses telling me they cannot cancel my membership as it is past the 30 day trial. I only saw past the 30 day trial cause a representative said they are working on it. Now I can only get in contact with an AI. I can’t look at any of my data, use the coach feature, use the blood pressure feature (the reason I got the higher end model).

This product is a scam wrapped in a health band. Would much prefer Apple Watch or garmin where I can actually access the data I am paying for. 

If a human being is reading this, please reach out to me on my email for a solution.

What happened to the Blood pressure tracking im Whoop app? Woke up one morning and it simply had disappeared. Jury is still out on whoop. Wish that I could see more metrics on temp, HRV, O2 sat, etc like other data graphs vs just a average of the data. My 3 year Samsung watch at least gives me this data (and not $349 a yr). Whoop does this for all other metrics (almost in overload.

I give this product zero stars because it is a low-quality device—cheap, inaccurate, unreliable, and simply not fit for purpose.

From the first day, I reported serious issues with core features such as ECG and blood pressure, which do not work at all. These are not minor features—they are exactly why someone would pay for a WHOOP membership. Despite raising these issues early, nothing was fixed.

Basic functionality is also unacceptable. I walk around 10,000 steps daily, yet the device records nothing while I am walking unless I manually log the activity. That completely defeats the purpose of using a wearable tracker.

The overall experience feels like using a product that is far behind the market standard, both in hardware quality and software performance. It is nowhere near the level of competitors like Apple Watch or Oura.

Customer support makes things worse. Responses is an AI automated and repetitive, with no real effort to resolve the actual problem. Instead of fixing issues, they redirect to generic troubleshooting steps that do not work.

WHOOP even granted me an additional one-month credit, which clearly acknowledges there were unresolved issues. Yet when I requested a refund, they refused, relying strictly on policy rather than addressing the fact that the product never worked properly from the start.

In summary:
	•Core features do not function properly
	•Tracking is highly inaccurate
	•Product quality is poor
	•Support is inhuman and ineffective and unhelpful
	•Refund handling is unfair

This is not a premium product. It is an underperforming device sold with a subscription model that does not deliver on its promises.

I do not recommend it.

I really loved Whoop…at first. To be honest, I still want to. They do a great job with data visualization and using AI to motivate users to adopt healthier habits. Sounds great right? And it is….until something goes wrong. 

Good luck solving any issues. Because their customer service is THE ABSOLUTE WORST!!!

I’ve been trying diligently for 6 weeks to fix an issue with my Whoop Advanced Labs subscription after my very first round of bloodwork failed to finish updating in the promised 7-10 day timeframe. Actually that seems generous, considering that I actually took the test SIXTEEN WEEKS AGO. I know I’m a procrastinating disaster of a human, but I thought it would work itself out in time and all would be well if I was patient. Huge mistake. 

The subscription promised to give me a health report after that 7-10 days to detail what changes you might implement to improve your next labs. Still haven’t seen that, can’t book my next round of labs until it does. And despite countless emails over more than 6 weeks, nothing has changed. 

Whoop: you have turned your biggest fan into a harsh critic. You should really do better by your premium subscribers.
You can’t swipe up to blood pressure insights on the health tab in the last two versions it just hangs. Fix it please.

I simply want the data from the lab test I have done input into my app.  I am so disheartened at the lack of concern or interest into my situation.

I wish I could give a zero. Two plus months of trying to get the results from the blood test I purchased. After going around in circles after almost 10 emails I noticed the responses were the same. I concluded that it’s AI Slop and no help whatsoever. I canceled my account. There are other choices.

ekg not functional blood pressure not accurate sleep metrics accuracy is questionable

Whoop has many cool features and awesome things to try like the ecg, blood pressure measure etc. it’s just too bad they don’t work. They might as well put “finds nearby unicorns”. Sick if it worked right? 100%. But it wouldn’t and it doesn’t. That’s whoop. I still get angry when I think about that I prepaid 12 months for this piece of garbage. Do yourself a favor and save yourself hours and hours of frustration by not buying this. I’d recommend making a nice beach fireplace and preferably just throw your money in there if you have too much of it. There’s no need to purchase bonus headaches, there’s plenty of free ones out there. If anyone employed at whoop reads this, which i doubt since they don’t read your own inbox (I’ve emailed twice with no response MONTHS AGO) then please just know that everyone makes mistakes and as there seemingly was a way back for Grima Wormtongue there’s a way back for you as well. I look more forward to my subscription ending than all the birthdays and xmases ever combined (included pre my birth). 

TLDR: it sucks. RUN THE OPPOSITE DIRDCTION
amazing app. i use 5.0 Life. MG. check my ECG every morning. input manual BP monthly. to calibrate.

overall app is an interesting way to keep track of various biomarkers. heart rate monitor during activities is unacceptable inaccurate (says i am at 140 when I am actually at 100, for example). can't log weightlifting exercises during the activity, so need to remember and log after the fact. does not import android health connect data reliably from Samsung health data and oxilife scale. actual ekg measures are correct and discern heart rhythms accurately. decent beginning, ready for improvement

I have been using Whoop from 2024 and i have never been facing issues with it. Mainly i use it for My sleep, strain and stress and this has been accurate compared to the other smatwatches. I give this product zero stars because it is a low-quality device—cheap, inaccurate, unreliable, and simply not fit for purpose.

From the first day, I reported serious issues with core features such as ECG and blood pressure, which do not work at all. These are not minor features—they are exactly why someone would pay for a WHOOP membership. Despite raising these issues early, nothing was fixed.

Basic functionality is also unacceptable. I walk around 10,000 steps daily, yet the device records nothing while I am walking unless I manually log the activity. That completely defeats the purpose of using a wearable tracker.

The overall experience feels like using a product that is far behind the market standard, both in hardware quality and software performance. It is nowhere near the level of competitors like Apple Watch or Oura.

Customer support makes things worse. Responses is an AI automated and repetitive, with no real effort to resolve the actual problem. Instead of fixing issues, they redirect to generic troubleshooting steps that do not work.

WHOOP even granted me an additional one-month credit, which clearly acknowledges there were unresolved issues. Yet when I requested a refund, they refused, relying strictly on policy rather than addressing the fact that the product never worked properly from the start.

In summary:
	•Core features do not function properly
	•Tracking is highly inaccurate
	•Product quality is poor
	•Support is inhuman and ineffective and unhelpful
	•Refund handling is unfair

This is not a premium product. It is an underperforming device sold with a subscription model that does not deliver on its promises.

I do not recommend it.

I’ve really enjoyed using WHOOP overall, but there are a few areas where I think it could be significantly better.

What I love:

The UI/UX is excellent. The app feels modern, sleek, and very tech-forward. I genuinely enjoy going through it every morning because everything is intuitive, easy to understand, and presented in a way that feels premium. WHOOP does a great job taking a lot of health and fitness data and making it approachable without feeling overwhelming.

I’ve also been impressed with the Recovery score. Most mornings, my recovery has lined up surprisingly well with how I actually feel when I wake up. That’s probably the feature I’ve found most valuable.

Where it falls short:

The WHOOP Coach/AI needs improvement. There have been times when its recommendations didn’t seem to match either my recovery data or how I was feeling. One morning I woke up feeling pretty run down with a 50% yellow recovery, yet WHOOP Coach essentially told me to train as usual. Bevel, using much of the same underlying health data, recommended that I take it easy and prioritize recovery. I followed Bevel’s recommendation, rested, and had a great recovery score the following day.

Obviously, one example doesn’t prove one recommendation was definitively better, but it made me much less confident in WHOOP Coach. For a product built so heavily around recovery, I’d like the AI to be more conservative and context-aware when recovery is mediocre and the user reports feeling poorly.

Sleep detection has also been disappointing compared with my Apple Watch. One night this past week, I was awake for roughly two hours in the middle of the night. My Apple Watch correctly detected that extended period of wakefulness, while WHOOP essentially treated it as a near-perfect night of sleep. That’s a pretty significant miss for a device where sleep is such an important part of the overall experience and Recovery score. For the amount of money Whoop costs you’d think the sleep detection would be on par with the Apple Watch. 

Overall, I really like WHOOP. The design, presentation of data, and Recovery experience are some of the best I’ve used. But for me, the AI coaching and sleep/wake detection need to catch up with the rest of the product. If WHOOP can improve those two areas, the overall experience would be much harder to beat. For the price I’d expect better quality. Especially since there are other apps that do similar things for less money.

ai_positive_reception.text: I've really enjoyed using Whoop. I think it provides interesting and beneficial insight without being overly complicated or time consuming. the AI feature is also well integrated and I consult it often. I recommend woop.

Love this app and device. I have the base level newest model. It’s awesome for tracking my fitness, sleep, and recovery. I primarily use the strength trainer with the AI coach and my results are awesome.

Many people complain about the cost of Whoop, but I find that I get great data and insights from the app and the AI interface. It really helps me understand my recovery from exercise, how well I’m sleeping, how my eating patterns affect my sleep and recovery. It’s been really great.

I love my Whoop band! It helps me to stay motivated and gives me clear insights into my health. The AI is getting better and they are putting a lot of effort into developing the product/app more.

My main issues are is that I feel like there are multiple features that you would think are basic features for a health device that are missing. For example, I have to track activities twice. Once in the actual activity section and then another time in my daily journal. It seems like the activity section should automatically update the Journal so you don’t have to repeat efforts speaking of the activity section, there are times where it misses the activity that I’m doing, especially low strength, activities like blah, blah blah, remember there are times when I’m sitting on the couch and open my app to 15 potential activity spotted messages. Also, the app doesn’t track basic things like blood oxygen levels throughout the day. Want to see the average lifespan of your battery? Sorry, can’t see that. Wanna ask the AI the average length of your dog walks, running, or other physical activity? Sorry, even though it attracts the data attracts your route, you are unable to see this either. Lastly, all the replacement bands are $100 or more. My band that I have now, which is my original band that I came with, desperately needs to be replaced, but because there are no cost-effective replacement I have yet to pull the trigger.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. I love the band, which is fairly comfortable and looks good, the WHOOP support team are very responsive and efficient, who is amazing at giving you daily strained targets that feel accurate and attainable, but still push you for training, and the app does genuinely encourage me to look at it each day, which helps with me staying consistent with my daily goals. I do really like the way. The AI is developing as well, being more responsive and being able to help with setting goals and adjusting goals as necessary based on what’s going on in life. 

Well, there are a lot of things that need to be developed or fixed, I would still highly recommend the WHOOP to anybody looking for a Fitness device. The speed at which WHOOP developing their app and product gives me hope that the things that I’m asking for will one day soon be features and overall I really do love my WHOOP band. I would probably recommend it best for those who are already moderately active and looking to bring their fitness to the next level, those looking to track and maintain daily habits, or those who generally want more insights into their health. I do still think that other brands might be better for women looking to track their cycles in fertility, or for those who don’t want to wait for the features that I mentioned above.

As someone of a certain age… Closer to 60, then 50, it’s been harder to stay in shape with the various responsibilities of taking care of my mom, and age, dog, and helping college kids become responsible professionals. As well as maintaining those relationships that are truly important so with that being said, the WHOOP band has given me the needed motivation and assistance to stay on track. With the AI feature helping me understand what I’m doing right and what I’m doing wrong, it’s really created more balance in my life. Which honestly, I need. And at the end of the day or at the end of the week, I feel better both physically and mentally. So thank you.

I have use WHOOP for over seven years and I can’t imagine life without it. I’ve seen it developed into a tool that not only helps me with my workouts and recoveries but my every day life ! 

My father became suddenly ill and I found myself 1300 miles away from home without my CrossFit classes for over two months and WHOOP instructed me daily how to stay fit while I was taking care of my dad with only a resistance band.

I ask WHOOP questions from diet to exercise to rest and encouraged me to get my bio markers done !  It was simple to add previous blood test to my app. I’m glad I did. Not only did it tell me what they were but how to make them better. 

I don’t go anywhere without my WHOOP! I’ve worn it for over 2500 days and I plan to wear it to my grave. Let’s see how that works?! 😀

I really like it’s workout feature and AI, hence I keep using it. The only problem I have is with App’s UX, it’s not easy on the eye and checking simple things like steps is a bit over complicated. It’s annoying to see flash cards every day and my ocd kicks in to clean them. You should not make things difficult for users, give options and suggestions to make it more widget based, where user can pick and choose way easy.
Whoop has transformed how I view my work outs and plan my recovery. The insights and coach helps keep all my records

Prior to using WHOOP my average hours sleep was just under 5.5 hrs down from prior  year of just under 6 hrs per night since using WHOOP, my average hours per night is over 7.5 hrs. It has educated and improved my health by bringing metrics like HRV and accurate RHR as well as many others. It has assisted in my training to improve cardiovascular and body comp to address recently diagnosed sarcoidosis. I am healthier for using it and better informed with information and questioning its AI.

Having Whooping makes me healthier. I highly recommend.

I'm really enjoying the insight to my health, fitness, recovery, and the AI component to access & set up plans to improve in all components of my overall health & wellbeing.

I’ve been using WHOOP for a while, and I genuinely believe it offers one of the best recovery, sleep, and strain analysis platforms available. The app is beautifully designed, the insights are actionable, and the AI coaching is a great addition.

However, there’s one major issue that needs attention: calorie synchronization with Apple Health and Apple Watch. My Apple Watch consistently records significantly higher calorie expenditure, but once the data syncs with WHOOP, the calories are reduced by around 40%, despite both devices tracking the same activities. This creates confusion and reduces confidence in the reported metrics.

I understand different platforms use different algorithms for estimating calories, but the discrepancy is too large and should be addressed—or at least clearly explained within the app. Better transparency about how WHOOP calculates calorie burn compared to Apple Health would greatly improve the user experience. WHOOP supports Apple Health integration, so users naturally expect synced data to remain consistent or be clearly interpreted. (App Store⁠)

Overall, WHOOP is an excellent platform with outstanding recovery insights, but improving Apple Health synchronization and calorie accuracy would make it even better. I hope the development team prioritizes this in a future update.

The AI on WHOOP is also super beneficial and it’s always there if you have questions about bedtime or eating certain things or what you should be doing throughout your day. GET THE WHOOP. The best part is I still have the 4.0! So trust me, I’ll be upgrading to the 5.0 soon.

When I started using WHOOP, I was still 110 pounds overweight, my blood pressure was in the 170s over 110s, and my WHOOP age was 11 years older than my actual age. I’ve now been using WHOOP for about eight months and through the metrics goals and AI coaching ability. I have lowered my blood pressure 35 points systolic and 20 points diastolic, I’ve lost 54 pounds, and my WHOOP page is only 4 1/2 years older than my actual age. 

I want to be really clear that not WHOOP nor any other tool can do the work for you. 

But if you’re committed to eating healthy, moving Your Body becoming fit and active, is the way to push yourself to your limit and stay healthy while doing it  

I’m also a new father, so my sleep is very unpredictable and I often wake up having gotten under four hours of sleep  

Wearing my WHOOP 24 seven has allowed me to understand on which days I can safely push myself and on which days I need to dial it back or rest  prior to using WHOOP it was all a guessing game and I would find myself getting sick frequently from overdoing it  

Now the only time that I get sick is when my daughter brings home something from daycare :) and even then WHOOP allows me to understand what I can safely do to continue push, pushing myself towards a healthier lifestyle on those days. 

If you were trying to become more fit, if you’re trying to get healthier, if you’re trying to lose weight or do anything to improve your health in your life, I highly highly highly recommend getting WHOOP and using the subscription model that allows for all of the features. It is worth the money 100%.
I’m a nerd when it comes to my health and the data I get from whoop is the best. They keep surprising me too with new features including Whoop AI, which is basically my best friend at this point.

This app and device have actually improved my life. I’m sleeping better and have been significantly more disciplined about my training, and it helps me with macro tracking as well. The built-in coach is fantastic, and I’m really impressed at the ability to upload pictures and files that help it maintain behavior. It seems to only get better with every update.

It’s even helped me in guarding me to go to the doctor in letting me know that I’m probably ill based on recent data. I think the coolest thing is that it attracts your sleep and educates you on every little bit of life and why sleep affects strain output and HRV and resting heart rate, etc

Not every day is a push day and whoop’s recovery features help me know when my body needs rest, so I don’t feel as if I’m just being lazy. Also so many new features like ECG, daily blood pressure readings, and whoop’s AI is such an intelligent use to better your health as opposed to ignorantly using AI to create memes and ask it silly things. I also participate in every study whoop has offered me, I love that they advance science. On top of scientific discovery, it also makes their product more accurate in the time I’ve used it (a big perk of the product is the accuracy). While the pricepoint is higher, as a preventative medicine professional (I’m an RN in biometric screenings) I firmly believe they are giving you sound data to improve your health day in and day out & make it well worth the price.

I have been a loyal WHOOP member for over six years and have recommended the product to countless friends, family members, athletes, and business colleagues. Unfortunately, my experience with their customer support has completely destroyed the trust I had in the company.

My account was deleted, resulting in the loss of approximately six years of health, recovery, training, and biometric data. For a company whose entire value proposition revolves around collecting and analyzing long-term personal health data, this is an unacceptable failure.

What made the situation even worse was the customer support experience. It took nearly two months of repeated emails and messages just to get meaningful responses and traction on the issue. The support process felt fragmented, slow, and heavily outsourced, with little ownership of the problem and no sense of urgency despite the severity of losing years of irreplaceable data.

After months of frustration, the resolution offered was two free months of service. To be clear, six years of personal health history cannot be replaced by two months of membership credit.

The most disappointing part is that I wasn’t a casual customer. I genuinely believed in WHOOP, paid for the service for years, and actively promoted it to others. Losing my data was devastating. Feeling ignored for two months while trying to get help was even worse.

The hardware and insights may be good when everything works, but a company’s true character is revealed when something goes wrong. Based on my experience, WHOOP’s customer support and account recovery processes fell far short of what customers should expect from a premium subscription service.

I sincerely hope WHOOP improves its support systems, data protection practices, and escalation procedures so that no other long-term member has to go through what I experienced.

The customer service experience has been equally frustrating. Finding support is difficult, getting help takes too long, and there is no simple way to resolve issues quickly.

The return process is another major problem. Customers are expected to pay for return shipping, and accessories cannot be returned through a simple online process. Instead, you have to contact customer support first, which is unnecessarily complicated and time-consuming.

I give this product zero stars because it is a low-quality device—cheap, inaccurate, unreliable, and simply not fit for purpose.

From the first day, I reported serious issues with core features such as ECG and blood pressure, which do not work at all. These are not minor features—they are exactly why someone would pay for a WHOOP membership. Despite raising these issues early, nothing was fixed.

Basic functionality is also unacceptable. I walk around 10,000 steps daily, yet the device records nothing while I am walking unless I manually log the activity. That completely defeats the purpose of using a wearable tracker.

The overall experience feels like using a product that is far behind the market standard, both in hardware quality and software performance. It is nowhere near the level of competitors like Apple Watch or Oura.

Customer support makes things worse. Responses is an AI automated and repetitive, with no real effort to resolve the actual problem. Instead of fixing issues, they redirect to generic troubleshooting steps that do not work.

WHOOP even granted me an additional one-month credit, which clearly acknowledges there were unresolved issues. Yet when I requested a refund, they refused, relying strictly on policy rather than addressing the fact that the product never worked properly from the start.

In summary:
	•Core features do not function properly
	•Tracking is highly inaccurate
	•Product quality is poor
	•Support is inhuman and ineffective and unhelpful
	•Refund handling is unfair

This is not a premium product. It is an underperforming device sold with a subscription model that does not deliver on its promises.

support_satisfaction.text:
I love my Whoop band! It helps me to stay motivated and gives me clear insights into my health. The AI is getting better and they are putting a lot of effort into developing the product/app more.

My main issues are is that I feel like there are multiple features that you would think are basic features for a health device that are missing. For example, I have to track activities twice. Once in the actual activity section and then another time in my daily journal. It seems like the activity section should automatically update the Journal so you don’t have to repeat efforts speaking of the activity section, there are times where it misses the activity that I’m doing, especially low strength, activities like blah, blah blah, remember there are times when I’m sitting on the couch and open my app to 15 potential activity spotted messages. Also, the app doesn’t track basic things like blood oxygen levels throughout the day. Want to see the average lifespan of your battery? Sorry, can’t see that. Wanna ask the AI the average length of your dog walks, running, or other physical activity? Sorry, even though it attracts the data attracts your route, you are unable to see this either. Lastly, all the replacement bands are $100 or more. My band that I have now, which is my original band that I came with, desperately needs to be replaced, but because there are no cost-effective replacement I have yet to pull the trigger.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. I love the band, which is fairly comfortable and looks good, the WHOOP support team are very responsive and efficient, who is amazing at giving you daily strained targets that feel accurate and attainable, but still push you for training, and the app does genuinely encourage me to look at it each day, which helps with me staying consistent with my daily goals. I do really like the way. The AI is developing as well, being more responsive and being able to help with setting goals and adjusting goals as necessary based on what’s going on in life. 

Well, there are a lot of things that need to be developed or fixed, I would still highly recommend the WHOOP to anybody looking for a Fitness device. The speed at which WHOOP developing their app and product gives me hope that the things that I’m asking for will one day soon be features and overall I really do love my WHOOP band. I would probably recommend it best for those who are already moderately active and looking to bring their fitness to the next level, those looking to track and maintain daily habits, or those who generally want more insights into their health. I do still think that other brands might be better for women looking to track their cycles in fertility, or for those who don’t want to wait for the features that I mentioned above.

I purchased WHOOP expecting a premium product and premium service, but my experience has been frustrating from the very beginning.

After only a few days of use, the app stopped working properly. One morning, my recovery never processed, the app remained stuck on the previous day, and my data would not update correctly. For a product that is supposed to provide real-time health and recovery insights, this is unacceptable.

The customer service experience has been equally frustrating. Finding support is difficult, getting help takes too long, and there is no simple way to resolve issues quickly.

The return process is another major problem. Customers are expected to pay for return shipping, and accessories cannot be returned through a simple online process. Instead, you have to contact customer support first, which is unnecessarily complicated and time-consuming.

For a company charging premium prices and a membership fee, I expected a polished product, reliable software, and responsive customer support. Instead, I experienced app issues within the first week, poor customer service, and a frustrating return process.

This has been one of the worst experiences I’ve had with a wearable technology company, and I would not recommend WHOOP to others.

I love the in-depth data and logging, but whoops seriously fumbled with this app. 

I am a professional UI & UX consultant who has worked with over 700 companies.

Whoop’s app is not intuitive or user friendly, and its implementation of its AI features are occasionally useful but the W ai logo covers the spot where the “+” SHOUKD be to add workouts. 

Also the color scheme is difficult to read and feels like a melted pool of dark similar colors. 

Accessing data is difficult and not intuitive or user friendly, and the lack of a “swipe back” from the left edge of the screen shows that whatever software intern was in charge of this app really forgot some basics unfortunately. 

The app also lacks a clear social interaction. It’s downright difficult to find and add friends. 

Weekly strain champions doesn’t even show the date when they win, just a generic timestamp with a 12-hr time and no date. 

The sleep tracker on average misses 2-3 days of sleep by at least 2 hours. 

I will gladly update my one star rating when the app is fixed but given the fact that 3-4 screenless fitness trackers are about to debut this year with significantly better UI/UX, I could easily see Whoop going under due to such a poorly laid out app interface.

Where to start…
I started with the Whoop 3.0 and liked it’s features and easy to use. Bought 18 month subscription and $200 in straps and batteries. 45 days later 4.0 comes out and is free and all gear I bought is obsolete! No notice. No refund. 

1. Whoop also double dips. Charge $30/ month for service then sells our info “anonymously” for more profit!! Why so expensive then!
2. Constant hardware issues. Battery doesn’t fully charge Whoop and could not get a spare battery for 8+ months. Battery updates have come out with no resolve so proves there is a known issue. 
3. Customer service is horrible and wants to just replace unit for every issue but only complimentary first time. Also takes time to respond but then wants to close ticket within 24 hours if you don’t respond asap. 
4. If you are serious about using this to work out, real time data is important. In version 4.0 constant data sync issues. I wake up and takes 1-2 hours for info to update. How can I know where my body is at and plan my day/ workout with that? I’m paying for this info too at a premium. 
5. App AI is confusing to navigate and overwhelming. Once you figure it out another update comes out and you start all over again. 

Bottom line, Whoop started off strong and great info for athletes. As of late it’s about profits and growing it’s wearables line but app and hardware have dropped wayside. I’m not renewing subscription and sad to see such a great source of info fail slowly.

Dear WHOOP, the world doesn’t need another running wearable!!! 

I have been a WHOOP user for a long time. After I got deeply frustrated with the 5.0, I cancelled my membership. About a year and a half later, I decided to sign up for a month hoping they did some major updates to the strength trainer section…NOPE.

The WHOOP was the first/only wearable that I found to track my strain/HRV in the weight room. I started with gen 2 and have used every version except the WHOOP Life. I have the 5.0 MG, and all throughout my use of the WHOOP, I have been hoping for updates to the strength trainer section of the app. I provide tons of feedback anytime I get a survey. They have never improved the UI of the strength trainer section, and it’s THE ONLY THING that sets this expensive wearable apart from my Garmin. Well, not anymore now that Garmin tracks strength training. Additionally, one of the key elements of the expense was that you would never have to pay for upgrades. You paid ~$450/year, so you get them. Not with the 5.0! The band is minutely smaller, so I have to get all new accessories because all the others don’t fit anymore; the charger won’t fit from my 4.0; the WHOOP 5.0 (not even considering the life/MG) is a costly “one-time” charge; and the strength training section still isn’t upgraded! I’m glad I paid for a month because it helped make my decision to stop using it feel more solid. It’s a shame, man, it feels like WHOOP wasted the one thing that set them apart.

If you’re looking for a wearable that goes beyond counting steps and actually helps you understand your body, I can’t recommend WHOOP enough. I’ve been a member for over seven years, and throughout that entire time I’ve never experienced any major  issue. It has been one of the most reliable pieces of technology I’ve ever owned.

What keeps me coming back year after year is the quality of the data. WHOOP doesn’t just collect information, it presents it in a way that helps you make better decisions. The recovery, sleep, strain, and health insights have become part of my daily routine and have genuinely helped me train smarter and recover better.

One of my favorite features is the Journal. Over the years, it has helped me identify patterns related to my sleep, recovery, diet, and daily habits that I never would have noticed otherwise. Being able to track behaviors and see how they impact my performance has made a huge difference in dialing in what works best for me personally.

As someone who spends a lot of time in the gym, another feature I absolutely love is the emphasis WHOOP has put on strength training and weightlifting. The Strength Trainer and muscular load tracking have been game changers. Instead of treating weightlifting like an afterthought, WHOOP actually measures the workload from sets, reps, and weight moved, giving a much more complete picture of training stress than traditional heart-rate-based trackers.  

After seven years, I still wear my WHOOP every day. The hardware is comfortable, the data is incredibly actionable, and the platform continues to evolve in ways that benefit serious fitness enthusiasts. For anyone who wants to better understand their recovery, improve their sleep, optimize their training, and make data-driven decisions about their health, WHOOP has been worth every penny.

The support team often seems either unwilling to properly troubleshoot the issue or lacking sufficient product knowledge, and the same can be said about phone support.

For someone whose schedule frequently changes, Whoop also seems unable to adapt properly. In comparison, my Apple Watch paired with Bevel handles changing schedules and data much better and provides a far more reliable experience.

I love my Whoop band! It helps me to stay motivated and gives me clear insights into my health. The AI is getting better and they are putting a lot of effort into developing the product/app more.

My main issues are is that I feel like there are multiple features that you would think are basic features for a health device that are missing. For example, I have to track activities twice. Once in the actual activity section and then another time in my daily journal. It seems like the activity section should automatically update the Journal so you don’t have to repeat efforts speaking of the activity section, there are times where it misses the activity that I’m doing, especially low strength, activities like blah, blah blah, remember there are times when I’m sitting on the couch and open my app to 15 potential activity spotted messages. Also, the app doesn’t track basic things like blood oxygen levels throughout the day. Want to see the average lifespan of your battery? Sorry, can’t see that. Wanna ask the AI the average length of your dog walks, running, or other physical activity? Sorry, even though it attracts the data attracts your route, you are unable to see this either. Lastly, all the replacement bands are $100 or more. My band that I have now, which is my original band that I came with, desperately needs to be replaced, but because there are no cost-effective replacement I have yet to pull the trigger.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. I love the band, which is fairly comfortable and looks good, the WHOOP support team are very responsive and efficient, who is amazing at giving you daily strained targets that feel accurate and attainable, but still push you for training, and the app does genuinely encourage me to look at it each day, which helps with me staying consistent with my daily goals. I do really like the way. The AI is developing as well, being more responsive and being able to help with setting goals and adjusting goals as necessary based on what’s going on in life. 

Well, there are a lot of things that need to be developed or fixed, I would still highly recommend the WHOOP to anybody looking for a Fitness device. The speed at which WHOOP developing their app and product gives me hope that the things that I’m asking for will one day soon be features and overall I really do love my WHOOP band. I would probably recommend it best for those who are already moderately active and looking to bring their fitness to the next level, those looking to track and maintain daily habits, or those who generally want more insights into their health. I do still think that other brands might be better for women looking to track their cycles in fertility, or for those who don’t want to wait for the features that I mentioned above.

I was someone who was mildly impressed with the Apple Watch and I really didn’t find it functional. I also struggled to charge it and put it back on and there were significant gaps in my data in the day time. Also, tracking sleep was something that was important to me and if I’m wearing my watch in the day and I have to charge it at night, I’m losing all the data. Tracking my menstrual cycle was something that I also wanted to do and when I was gifted WHOOP for my birthday from my boyfriend I put it on and committed incredibly. I now have over 400 days of consistent data. I have been working to decrease my health age while also tracking my cycles with great detail and I will be enrolling in advanced labs in the next year to get my bio markers for any health concerns.

I’m a very active middle aged person who adopted Whoop to track my multitude of activities. I’ve encountered a major problem: Whoop doesn’t accurately measure where most of us live our lives: in HR zones 0-2. For a 5 mile walk in 85*F heat, whoop recorded 150 calories. Why? ‘I wasn’t working hard enough.’ The AI agent was condescending, passive aggressive and deflective. So, if you aren’t regularly pushing yourself often at HR zones 4-5, Whoop is basically useless for you.
